description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Theory of Machines topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: theory-of-machines

facts.claim: Lower pairs have surface contact; higher pairs point or line contact

source.quote: A lower pair is one in which there occurs a surface or area contact between two members

facts.claim: A kinematic pair constrains relative motion of two links

source.quote: a connection between two physical objects that imposes constraints on their relative movement

facts.claim: Mobility formula counts DOF from links and joints

source.quote: computes the number of parameters that define the configuration of a linkage from the number of links and joints

facts.claim: Joints remove degrees of freedom

source.quote: Joints that connect bodies in this system remove degrees of freedom and reduce mobility

facts.claim: The four-bar is the simplest closed-chain linkage

source.quote: a four-bar linkage, also called a four-bar, is the simplest closed-chain movable linkage

facts.claim: A crank is a link that can make a full revolution (Grashof: s + l ≤ p + q)

source.quote: A link connecting to the ground by a revolute joint that can perform a complete revolution is called a crank link

facts.claim: Slider-crank: three revolute joints and one sliding (prismatic) joint

source.quote: a four-link mechanism with three revolute joints and one prismatic (sliding) joint

facts.claim: Converts rotation of the crank into linear motion of the slider (and back)

source.quote: the rotation of the crank drives the linear movement of the slider

facts.claim: The instantaneous centre is the point of zero velocity

source.quote: is a point that has zero vel

facts.claim: Coriolis acceleration appears for motion in a rotating frame (2ωv)

source.quote: acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame

facts.claim: Gears trade torque for speed

source.quote: gears and gear trains can be used to trade torque for rotational speed between two axles

facts.claim: A small gear driving a larger one increases torque and reduces speed

source.quote: When a small gear drives a larger one, the mechanical advantage of this ideal lever causes the torque T to increase but the rotational speed

facts.claim: Helical gear teeth are set at an angle to the axis

source.quote: In a helical or dry fixed gear the tooth walls are not parallel to the axis of rotation, but are set at an angle

facts.claim: Sun, planet (on a carrier) and ring gears

source.quote: A carrier connects the centers of the two gears and rotates to carry the planet gear(s) around the sun gear

facts.claim: Planets may mesh with an outer ring (annulus) gear

source.quote: an outer gear ring, or ring gear, sometimes called an annulus gear

facts.claim: A flywheel stores rotational energy ½Iω²

source.quote: uses the conservation of angular momentum to store rotational energy

facts.claim: It absorbs excess and releases energy to smooth speed fluctuations

source.quote: will donate a surge in power output upon a drop in power input and will conversely absorb any excess power input

facts.claim: Vibration is oscillation about an equilibrium

source.quote: vibration (from Latin vibrāre 'to shake') is an oscillation of matter about an equilibrium point

facts.claim: Forced response occurs at the forcing frequency

source.quote: is equal to the frequency of the applied force or motion

facts.claim: Critical speed = speed matching the natural frequency (resonance)

source.quote: When the rotational speed is equal to the natural frequency, then that speed is referred to as a critical speed
